papers.title: Bridging the QC–QA Cognitive Handoff: An Agentic Verification Harness for Error Detection, Specification Cross-Checking and Quality Documentation Assembly in Pharmaceutical Quality Assurance
papers.summary: Abstract Background. Quality control (QC) results reach regulatory dossiers through manual transcription and review. Such a benchmark does not yet exist. No collection of pharmaceutical quality documents carries discrepancies of known class and location, so automated verification cannot yet be evaluated against measured performance across realistic transfer errors and document types. Objectives. To specify (i) an architecture in which large language models only read and propose values, deterministic code performs every calculation and acceptance test, and a qualified reviewer makes every decision; (ii) a protocol for building a reference corpus and evaluating such systems; and (iii) sensitivity estimates from three dossiers. The plan covers design, evaluation, and measurement. Methods. Records from three ASEAN Common Technical Dossier Part II submissions (13, 14 and 10 records) were de-identified, and 112, 100 and 120 discrepancies across nine classes were introduced into dossiers A, B and C. A finding counted as a detection when it identified an injected discrepancy at the correct location with the correct class. The framework ran blind to the register. Sensitivity to injected discrepancies is reported per dossier with Wilson 95% confidence intervals and pooled by random-effects meta-analysis; clustering within records is not accounted for. Results. papers.title: An auditable multi-agent forum for scientific workflows with a computational MOF case study
papers.summary: Scientific research increasingly combines large language models, computational tools and automated laboratories, creating a need to link hypotheses, assumptions, artifacts and revisions. We present Core-Forum, a persistent multi-agent forum architecture designed to organize these records in a common research thread. Its agent-package specification separates role kernels, model bindings, knowledge sources, tool permissions, artifact schemas and validation obligations. Retained interfaces illustrate role organization and protocol/artifact handoff; they do not establish a sample-linked MOF laboratory experiment or a controlled evaluation of the architecture. The quantitative case study instead reuses database-derived MOF pore descriptors and gas-uptake records. A corrected bounded geometric closure defines the dimensionless coordinate D W , while a fixed-radius unit-cell index D L supplies a comparative structural summary. Across 155,600 name-deduplicated admissible records, the fixed-radius association has R² = 0.4967. Sensitivity scenarios and within-gas holdout baselines delimit descriptor utility. D W is a deterministic nonlinear transformation of its geometric inputs, not a universal adsorption predictor. This study presents a workflow design and reproducible computational case; experimental closed-loop discovery and multi-agent performance gains remain to be evaluated.

papers.title: Self-directed coaching: repositioning the client as the internalizing agent of developmental self-regulation a conceptual framework and research agenda for coaching theory and practice
papers.summary: Coaching has become one of the most widely deployed developmental interventions in organizational, educational, and health-professions settings, and the literature offers substantial evidence for its short-term benefits. Evidence on whether those benefits persist after formal coaching support is withdrawn is thinner and less systematic, and the question points to an unresolved tension at the field’s core. Coaching is justified by its capacity to build independent, self-regulating professionals, but it is typically structured in a way that locates diagnosis, goal setting, strategic planning, and accountability in the coach rather than the client. The result can be improvement that does not outlive the engagement. This paper introduces Self-Directed Coaching (SDC) as a theory-based framework that repositions the client as the principal agent of their own developmental regulation. Grounded in self-determination theory, intentional change theory, regulatory focus theory, self-directed and self-regulated learning, cybernetic control theory, and attachment theory, SDC reframes coaching as a scaffolded process whose intended end-state is reduced dependence on formal coaching support. The framework’s central mechanism is self-regulatory internalization, the progressive transfer of coaching functions from an external agent to the client’s own regulatory repertoire. papers.title: The Inverse-Wisdom Law: Architectural Tribalism and the Consensus Paradox in Agentic Swarms
papers.summary: Abstract As AI transitions toward multi-agent systems (MAS), research paradigms operate on the assumption that agent collaboration mirrors the ''Wisdom of the Crowd.'' We challenge this assumption by formalizing the \textit{Consensus Paradox}, a phenomenon in which agentic swarms prioritize internal agreement over logical truth. Through 36 experiments with 12,804 trajectories across three benchmarks (GAIA, Multi-Challenge, and SWE-bench) and three state-of-the-art (SOTA) model families (Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and GPT-5.4), we derive and empirically validate the \textit{Inverse-Wisdom Law}. In kinship-dominant swarms, adding agents increases the stability of erroneous trajectories rather than the probability of truth. The introduction of additional logical audits converges the system toward a \textit{Cascade Point} where internal disagreement entropy hits zero while factual error hits unity. Across 12 family configurations of a three-agent chain, we establish the \textit{Architectural Tribalism Asymmetry} as a reproducible inference-time property of the model family that synthesizes the final answer. We demonstrate that terminal swarm integrity is strictly gated by the synthesizer's receptive logic rather than aggregate agent quality. A homogeneous Gemini swarm reached this Cascade Point in $100\%$ of Multi-Challenge trajectories. Even when the reviewing agent reject

papers.title: Safe Recovery of AI Agents in Enterprise Systems: Preventing Duplicate Actions and Preserving Human Corrections
papers.summary: Reliable use of AI agents in enterprise systems depends on what happens after an action fails or its outcome becomes uncertain. Retrying can duplicate an order, while reversing a workflow can invalidate a person’s subsequent correction. The central challenge is deciding whether recovery is justified by the available evidence and still satisfies the business request. We investigate this challenge in a reproducible testbed connecting order, inventory and billing services with different API guarantees. Controlled failures and concurrent edits reveal two evaluation gaps: protecting individual records does not ensure consistency across related services, and preserving an edit does not ensure that the final workflow fulfils its instruction. A separate diagnostic identified nine apparent completions that left human instructions unsatisfied. A conventional recovery implementation with equivalent safeguards matched the evaluated controller in all 270 paired runs, locating the observed benefit in shared engineering protections rather than a distinct recovery algorithm. On the prospective test configurations, both completed 108 of 180 runs without scored violations and left 72 for manual resolution. These findings provide a practical basis for evaluating agent integrations: verify uncertain effects, check related records, and distinguish completed business goals from unresolved handoffs.

papers.title: Post-Training on the Clock: Specializing a Small Language Model on a Consumer GPU
papers.summary: Abstract How should a language model be specialized for a target task when training is limited to one consumer GPU and a few hours? We study the allocation of a nominal three-hour training budget, with up to 0.3 additional hours, between supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). We use tool calling as a case study because of its practical relevance to language-model agents and its verifiable outputs. Using Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct with low-rank adaptation on an RTX 5060 Ti with 16 GB of memory, we compare SFT, GRPO, and six sequential SFT-to-GRPO allocations. Training uses a filtered mixture of xLAM function-calling examples and Hammer irrelevance examples, covering both call construction and abstention when no offered tool is suitable. Evaluation reports xLAM exact tool-call and function-name accuracies for local call construction, BFCL-v3 Single-turn FC (agg) for external function calling, BFCL-v3 Irrelevance (agg) for abstention, and MMLU, MATH-500, and IFEval for selected general capabilities. The suffix (agg) denotes study-specific averages of selected subset accuracies weighted by subset size. At the last evaluated checkpoints within 3.3 reported hours, SFT achieves the highest xLAM exact tool-call accuracy (82.82%), compared with 69.13% for GRPO alone. Selected hybrid allocations improve external function-calling accuracy over SFT, with dif

papers.title: Navigating the Mirage: A Dual-Path Agentic Framework for Robust Misleading Chart Question Answering
papers.summary: Despite the success of Vision-Language Models (VLMs), misleading charts remain a significant challenge due to their deceptive visual structures and distorted data representations. We present ChartCynics, an agentic dual-path framework designed to unmask visual deception via a "skeptical" reasoning paradigm. Unlike holistic models, ChartCynics decouples perception from verification: a Diagnostic Vision Path captures structural anomalies (e.g., inverted axes) through strategic ROI cropping, while an OCR-Driven Data Path ensures numerical grounding. To resolve cross-modal conflicts, we introduce an Agentic Summarizer optimized via a two-stage protocol: Oracle-Informed SFT for reasoning distillation and Deception-Aware GRPO for adversarial alignment. This pipeline effectively penalizes visual traps and enforces logical consistency. Evaluations on two benchmarks show that ChartCynics achieves 74.43% and 64.55% accuracy, providing an absolute performance boost of ~29% over the Qwen3-VL-8B backbone, outperforming state-of-the-art proprietary models. Our results demonstrate that specialized agentic workflows can grant smaller open-source models superior robustness, establishing a new foundation for trustworthy chart interpretation.

papers.title: MetaNav: Metacognitive Vision-Language Navigation via Reflective Exploration
papers.summary: Training-free Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) agents powered by foundation models can follow instructions and explore 3D environments. However, existing approaches rely on greedy frontier selection and passive spatial memory, leading to inefficient behaviors such as local oscillation and redundant revisiting. We argue that this stems from a lack of metacognitive capabilities: the agent cannot monitor its exploration progress, diagnose strategy failures, or adapt accordingly. To address this, we propose MetaNav, a metacognitive navigation agent integrating spatial memory, history-aware planning, and reflective correction. Spatial memory builds a persistent 3D semantic map. History-aware planning penalizes revisiting to improve efficiency. Reflective correction detects stagnation and uses an LLM to generate corrective rules that guide future frontier selection. Experiments on GOAT-Bench, HM3D-OVON, and A-EQA show that MetaNav achieves state-of-the-art performance while reducing VLM queries by 20.7%, demonstrating that metacognitive reasoning significantly improves robustness and efficiency.

papers.title: Supporting engagement, behavior change, and equitable self-management in menstrual and menopausal health: A multi-agent digital-health framework
papers.summary: Menstrual-cycle-related conditions and, later, menopausal symptoms are highly prevalent across the female life course and impose a large, under-recognized burden on quality of life and work, yet digital tools to support self-management are fragmented, hard to sustain, and unevenly reached. We propose HERA (Health Engagement and Reflective Agent architecture), a conceptual, hypothesis-generating framework for supporting engagement, behavior change, and equitable self-management in menstrual and menopausal health across the life course. Under human governance, HERA combines two adaptive agents (interpretation and orchestration) with three rule-based modules (self-monitoring and data integration, guidance and content governance, and equity and engagement monitoring) that integrate self-monitoring, deliver personalized feedback, surface governed guidance, monitor equity, and coordinate hand-offs to clinicians and occupational-health services. Distinct from clinician-facing diagnostic agents, HERA is patient-facing and treats equity and engagement as first-class. We distinguish technically feasible from aspirational elements and set out a staged, threshold-gated evaluation plan. HERA is a design reference, not a validated system.

papers.title: Learning‐by‐twinning: Organizational digital twins and the future of search
papers.summary: Abstract Research Summary Entrepreneurs and managers often need to evaluate strategic choices, such as redesigning an incentive plan or entering an unfamiliar market, before committing scarce resources. Existing offline search tools, including mental models, analogical reasoning, model building, and simulation, allow managers to weigh alternatives without acting, but each is limited by what a single decision maker can specify, recall, or imagine. We argue that advances in generative AI, combined with the growing availability of firm‐specific digital trace data, are transforming this tradeoff. We introduce the organizational digital twin (ODT), an infrastructure combining firm‐specific data, AI‐based behavioral simulation models, and governance rules which facilitates a new form of offline search that we call learning‐by‐twinning: search conducted by observing how a strategic choice unfolds within a digital replica of the firm. We identify three mechanisms through which learning‐by‐twinning creates value, namely expanded search, safer experimentation, and richer system‐level feedback as well as specify certain conditions under which these benefits may attenuate. Managerial Summary Strategic entrepreneurship depends on discovering and refining opportunities through search and experimentation under uncertainty. papers.title: The impact of temporal resampling on the safety of clinical reinforcement learning: A simulated trial
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) is a type of artificial intelligence for making optimal choices. In healthcare, researchers generally use offline RL (ORL), where models are trained and evaluated from retrospective observational data. To accommodate naturally irregular clinical records, researchers often resample the data into uniform time intervals before training (known as binning). However, binning may create counterfactual trajectories that do not represent clinical practice. We first quantified these distortions in patients receiving continuous insulin infusions in the MIMIC-IV intensive care database. Binning reversed the apparent causal order for over 70% of paired glucose measurements and insulin adjustments within the same interval, and frequently masked significant dysglycaemic events and merged distinct treatment decisions together. We then conducted an in silico clinical trial using 30 virtual patients with type 1 diabetes from the FDA-approved UVA/Padova simulator. The simulator was modified to include stochastic intervals between decisions and used to generate a training dataset for offline RL. We trained three ORL algorithms on both the unprocessed dataset and equivalent datasets resampled at 10-minute, 2-hour, and 4-hour intervals. When deployed back into the simulated environment, temporal resampling was found to reduce model performance by up to 60% relative to unp

papers.title: Opioid overdose deaths are declining in Chicago, but not every neighborhood is seeing the same progress: JSAD research
papers.summary: This report focuses on opioid overdose deaths in the Black Chicago community -a vital factor in the fight for Black prosperity and equity.

papers.title: Rho: A Purpose-Driven Workspace for Human-AI Collaborative Analysis
papers.summary: Agent-assisted bioinformatics has moved the bottleneck from computing a result to judging it: whether a comparison answers the intended question, on which unit of replication, at which version of the input, and what would change the conclusion. These judgments need materials that are usually scattered across conversations, notebooks, figures, run logs and notes, while the agent's context is a transcript rather than the structure the researcher is actually reading. We present Rho, a human--AI collaborative analysis environment that organizes materials by the current scientific purpose: it selects or obtains the materials a judgment needs, declares the relations they serve, composes operable views, and makes this organization a shared state that is at once the researcher's reading interface and the agent's continuation context. We present the design in three parts: a method object---the operations that form a round-trip, the kinds of state that must stay distinct, and the protocol invariants that make each distinction checkable; a three-layer architecture that separates capability providers from the application that composes them; and five illustrative analyses on public data. papers.title: Viewpoints on inclusive education at the end of initial teacher preparation: Q methodology research
papers.summary: Abstract This study used Q methodology to explore the perspectives on inclusive education held by 44 student teachers completing their initial teacher education (ITE) programme at Qatar University. Participants ranked 44 statements along a quasi‐normal distribution; factor analysis yielded four distinct viewpoints. The first frames inclusion as a shared professional commitment owned by every teacher within a collaborative ecosystem. The second regards mainstream inclusion as structurally unrealistic and assigns responsibility primarily to specialist staff. The third is the most affirmative orientation, grounding inclusion in rights and expressing confidence in its outcomes and systemic feasibility. The fourth combines a genuine moral commitment to inclusion with a critical view that students with special needs are being inadequately supported and that teachers lack the preparation to address this. The coexistence of these four viewpoints within a single cohort that completed the same programme suggests that the current single‐course structure has not produced a coherent or shared professional framework for inclusive teaching. The programme appears to have established a normative baseline around inclusion as a principled commitment while leaving significant gaps in conceptual clarity, professional responsibility and practical readiness. These gaps carry direct implications for I

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: Can TDD improve the quality of LLM-migrated code? : A pilot study in an industrial context
papers.summary: The emergence of Large Language Models (LLM) has created new possibilities for automating software development, yet ensuring the quality of AI-generated code remains a major challenge. We aim to investigate if Test-Driven Development (TDD) can improve the quality of code generated by an LLM in a fully autonomous context, within a pilot project at Decerno AB. We added TDD to their pilot workflow, using a design science approach, with continuous refinements to prompt design and workflow structure, based on observed AI behavior. The generated code was evaluated and compared with non-TDD code, using SonarQube for static code analysis. The results indicate that TDD reduced complexity and code duplication, but introduced more quality issues overall, while non-TDD produced fewer, but more severe issues. The generated tests from the TDD workflow focused more on content verification than on behavioral testing, contributing to a lower code coverage per test compared to non-TDD. The findings suggest that TDD involves trade-offs that may favor certain development priorities, in particular where lower complexity and reduced duplication are more beneficial than minimizing total issue count. This indicates that a strict application of TDD may not be optimal in an autonomous AI-driven context, and that exploring more flexible adaptations of the TDD workflow remains interesting for future resea

papers.title: From Coding to Creativity: Integrating Design Thinking into IT and Technology Education
papers.summary: This study examines how the integration of Design Thinking into Information Technology (IT) and technology education can bridge technical programming skills and creative, human-centered problem-solving. Specifically, it explores how the five stages of Design Thinking empathizing, defining, ideating, prototyping, and testing shape students’ creative thinking, active engagement, and collaborative learning experiences. A qualitative research approach was employed, involving teachers, students, and school principals as key informants. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, classroom observations, and documentation of learning activities, then analyzed thematically to identify recurring patterns in teaching practices and student experiences. The findings indicate that Design Thinking creates opportunities for students to move beyond coding procedures toward developing digital solutions that respond to real users’ needs. Through collaborative ideation, iterative prototyping, and feedback-based testing, students demonstrate greater involvement in learning, explore alternative solutions, and communicate their ideas more actively. The approach also provides opportunities to develop empathy, creativity, collaboration, and a willingness to experiment with and revise initial designs. papers.title: Metacognitive Reasoning in Energy Based Models Using Instance Based Learning Theory
papers.summary: Metacognition involves reasoning about cognitive processes themselves. An example is in resource allocation where we choose how much time and effort to put into a reasoning task before we begin based on our confidence. Current Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems that rely on Large Language Models (LLMs) cannot estimate their uncertainty about an output without first responding, and cannot dynamically allocate resources to producing an output, making this type of metacognitive process difficult. A recently proposed alternative to classic transformer architectures that addresses these two concerns is the Energy Based Model (EBM) which allows for interpretable uncertainty modeling and dynamic allocation of compute resources. While EBMs can allow for control of these two processes, the actual metacognitive task of determining compute allocation based on uncertainty is not directly addressed. Instance-Based Learning Theory (IBLT) provides an approach to modeling human-like decisions from experience that has previously been applied to predicting human metacognitive reasoning. In this paper we introduce a framework for MEtacognitive Reasoning with Instance-based Learning Theory and Energy Dynamics (MERITED). Grounded in IBLT, this framework allows for control of the computational effort allocated in an EBM to allow for metacognitive control over reasoning effort based on uncertainty

papers.title: Interactive Digital Media-Assisted SSCS Learning: A Solution to Enhance Problem-Solving Ability and Alleviate Mathematics Anxiety
papers.summary: Problem-solving is a practical skill that students must master in 21st-century learning. However, various findings indicate that this capability remains low among junior high school students, who are beginning to study mathematical concepts in greater depth. Anxiety toward the subject matter, teachers, and mathematics instruction itself is a key factor influencing students' mathematical problem-solving performance. To address this, this study aims to examine the effect of the Search, Solve, Create, and Share (SSCS) learning model, a model that provides a clear roadmap for students to implement Polya's problem-solving steps, assisted by interactive digital media (PhET and Mathigon), on students' problem-solving ability and anxiety. This quasi-experimental study used a factorial design and included eighth-grade students. The research sample was selected using the cluster random sampling technique. Data were collected using a test instrument and a mathematics anxiety questionnaire and were subsequently analyzed using a two-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA). The results of the study indicate that: (1) Hypothesis testing showed that there was a significant effect of different learning models on students’ problem-solving ability, with Fobs (= 8.405) > Ftab (= 4.016). papers.title: Probe and Skip: Self-Predictive Token Skipping for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
papers.summary: Long-context inference enhances the reasoning capability of Large Language Models (LLMs), but incurs significant computational overhead. Token-oriented methods, such as pruning and skipping, have shown great promise in reducing inference latency, yet still suffer from inherently insufficient structure optimization, outdated selection criteria, and redundancy interference, resulting in suboptimal speed-accuracy trade-off. To address these issues, we propose a novel training-free framework dubbed Self-Predictive Token Skipping (SPTS), for efficient long-context LLM inference. Specifically, motivated by probing the influence of target layers prior to skipping, we design two selective token skipping strategies for typical structures, including Partial Attention Probing (PAP) for multi-head attention and Low-rank Transformation Probing (LTP) for feed forward network. The former selects informative tokens via partial forward attention computation, while the latter constructs a low-rank proxy network to predict token transformations. In addition, a Multi-Stage Delayed Pruning (MSDP) strategy reallocates skipping budgets and progressively removes redundant tokens across layers. Extensive experiments display the effectiveness of our method, achieving up to 2.46× and 2.29× speedups for prefilling and end-to-end generation, respectively, while maintaining state-of-the-art accuracy. papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. These include repetitive-strain injuries, sleep disruption, problematic gaming, and adverse mental-health and academic outcomes. Evidence concerning violent game

papers.title: An Assessment of Accessibility and Affordability of Inpatient Psychiatric Care in Tennessee
papers.summary: Introduction: Access to mental health has seen changes over the past decade, but little research and attention have been given to access to inpatient psychiatric facilities. Inpatient psychiatric care is crucial for patients experiencing mental health emergencies who need immediate access to care. Gaps in spatial accessibility, affordability, and the access and assessment process were identified due to a lack of available information in the field. Methods: Secondary data from the Tennessee Department of Health were used to assess financial accessibility through payer source charges and patient encounters, as well as through mapping of inpatient psychiatric facilities and conducting drive time and coverage area analyses. Primary data were collected through interviews with clinicians located in Northeastern Tennessee to gain insight into the assessment process and gather their perceptions of inpatient care. Results: Longitudinal descriptive reviews on the financial accessibility among Tennessee Inpatient Facilities. This showed increased variability among facilities when stratified by region, ownership, and type of operation. Spatial accessibility in ArcGIS showed 82% of counties were not covered within a 30-minute radius of inpatient facilities. Analysis showed that Middle Tennessee had significantly less coverage from inpatient facilities and raised concerns about spatial-socia

papers.title: Pieces Solving a Puzzle: Emerging Roles and Cross-Field Analogies During a Distributed Epistemic Game
papers.summary: In an effort to describe why some problems can’t be solved, a character compared them to a cubic meter of platinum - a block so dense that all the people who could squeeze around it still couldn’t lift it off the ground. In the same way, these problems simply can’t have enough people gathered around and communicating about them - and so they remain unsolved. This research looks at the first Polymath Project (2009) as an example of a distributed epistemic game to examine how groups engage with complex problems. and without a locally omniscient individual. In this setting of epistemic uncertainty, interactions between individuals reveal patterns of participation, and an analogy opens a new solution pathway by introducing a problem-solving approach from another field. These insights answer the initial question of the Polymath Project - ‘Is massively collaborative mathematics possible?’ - and offer hope for lifting the cubic meter of other unsolvable problems.

papers.title: Designing a Curriculum Model Based on Artificial Intelligence and Purposeful Physical Activity to Enhance Learning Self-Regulation, Mental Health, and Psychological Well-Being among Students
papers.summary: Objective: The objective of this study was to design and validate a curriculum model based on artificial intelligence and purposeful physical activity with emphasis on enhancing learning self-regulation, mental health, and psychological well-being among students. Methods and Materials: This applied developmental study was conducted using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. In the qualitative phase, 20 experts in curriculum studies, educational technology, artificial intelligence in education, physical education, educational psychology, and student mental health were selected through purposive criterion-based sampling from Tehran and participated in semi-structured interviews. The interview data were analyzed using thematic analysis to extract the main dimensions, components, and indicators of the proposed curriculum model. In the quantitative phase, 384 secondary school students from Tehran were selected through multistage cluster sampling during the 2025–2026 academic year. Data were collected using a researcher-made curriculum model validation questionnaire, a learning self-regulation questionnaire, the General Health Questionnaire, and a psychological well-being scale. papers.title: GPA-VGGT:Adapting VGGT to Large Scale Localization by Self-Supervised Learning with Geometry and Physics Aware Loss
papers.summary: Transformer-based general visual geometry frameworks have shown promising performance in camera pose estimation and 3D scene understanding. Recent advancements in Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer (VGGT) models have shown great promise in camera pose estimation and 3D reconstruction. However, these models typically rely on ground truth labels for training, posing challenges when adapting to unlabeled and unseen scenes. In this paper, we propose a self-supervised framework to train VGGT with unlabeled data, thereby enhancing its localization capability in large-scale environments. To achieve this, we extend conventional pair-wise relations to sequence-wise geometric constraints for self-supervised learning. Specifically, in each sequence, we sample multiple source frames and geometrically project them onto different target frames, which improves temporal feature consistency. We formulate physical photometric consistency and geometric constraints as a joint optimization loss to circumvent the requirement for hard labels. By training the model with this proposed method, not only the local and global cross-view attention layers but also the camera and depth heads can effectively capture the underlying multi-view geometry. papers.title: Tex3D: Objects as Attack Surfaces via Adversarial 3D Textures for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong performance in robotic manipulation, yet their robustness to physically realizable adversarial attacks remains underexplored. Existing studies reveal vulnerabilities through language perturbations and 2D visual attacks, but these attack surfaces are either less representative of real deployment or limited in physical realism. In contrast, adversarial 3D textures pose a more physically plausible and damaging threat, as they are naturally attached to manipulated objects and are easier to deploy in physical environments. Bringing adversarial 3D textures to VLA systems is nevertheless nontrivial. A central obstacle is that standard 3D simulators do not provide a differentiable optimization path from the VLA objective function back to object appearance, making it difficult to optimize through an end-to-end manner. To address this, we introduce Foreground-Background Decoupling (FBD), which enables differentiable texture optimization through dual-renderer alignment while preserving the original simulation environment. To further ensure that the attack remains effective across long-horizon and diverse viewpoints in the physical world, we propose Trajectory-Aware Adversarial Optimization (TAAO), which prioritizes behaviorally critical frames and stabilizes optimization with a vertex-based parameterization. papers.title: Navigating the Open-Source Model Ecosystem: An Empirical Study of Creator Practices in Artistic Image Generation
papers.summary: The open-sourcing of powerful image generation models has created a vibrant ecosystem where creators curate and combine a vast array of community-contributed models. This practice stands in sharp contrast to using closed-source tools like Midjourney. Yet, little is known about these emerging creative workflows. To bridge this gap, this paper presents the first large-scale empirical study of creator model usage behavior within this open-source image generation ecosystem. We construct a novel dataset of 6 million images with their embedded generation metadata -- a detailed recipe of the creation process, including the models used and the prompts. By linking the usage of 22.4K base models and 154K LoRA models to the images, our findings underscore the ecosystem's unique strengths and its inherent obstacles. This provides valuable insights for making this ecosystem more sustainable and innovative. Moreover, we make our dataset publicly available, providing creators with practical references for producing better artworks and researchers to facilitate further studies.
